newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine grain buyers seen sidelined - trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine grain buyers seen sidelined - trade.

text.p: Philippine grain importers are expected to shun the U.S. market next week, waiting for wheat prices to soften before resuming purchases, traders said on Wednesday.

Almost all flour company executives responsible for buying wheat had already left their offices by late Wednesday for the long Easter holidays. The Philippines celebrates Easter beginning on Thursday, March 27, through Sunday, March 30.
"So as long prices stay at these levels...buyers will continue to shy away," a senior Manila trader said.
Buyers may even opt for Canadian wheat due to high prices in the United States, the dealers said.
"The Philippines has been rejecting offers of U.S. wheat. We recently bought Canadian wheat and we may just go Canadian again. Anything beyond US$4 a bushel is not (being) accepted," one trader said.
The price of the May spring wheat futures contract in Minneapolis, where the Philippines buys most of its wheat, closed on Tuesday 5-1/4 U.S. cents up at $4.09-1/4 a bushel.
Philippine flour mills have turned to supplies from Canada, where they recently bought 35,000 tonnes of Canadian spring and soft wheat for May shipment.
"I don't see yet a big surge in buying next week. It will still be bearish until prices are lower," said another trader.
There will probably be no negotiations this week for rice and corn imports, the state-run National Food Authority (NFA) said.
But it said the Philippines may have to import another 350,000 to 450,000 tonnes of corn for animal feed to help fill a supply shortfall that analysts have forecast may reach one million tonnes.
The NFA said four vessels arrived this month with 45,200 tonnes of rice while three vessels carrying around 92,100 tonnes of Chinese corn recently docked in Manila.
The Philipines plans to import a total of 655,000 tonnes of rice during the seasonally lean third period of the year.
The Department of Trade and Industry said prices of local hard flour were unchanged at 290 pesos per 25-kg bag while soft flour was seen steady at 260 pesos per 25 kg bag.
The average retail price of yellow corn in the local market, however, slipped to 10.34 pesos a kg from last week's 10.77 pesos while white corn dropped to 10.35 pesos a klg from 10.94 pesos.
